The exact cause of the HTML response — whether a routing misconfiguration, a server-side error page, a redirect to a login/error page, or a deployment issue on the public share endpoint — cannot be determined from the supplied evidence alone.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Eval Failing: POST /api/agents Returns 409 Agent Quota Exceeded (limit is 100)
investigation.summary: The AURA observability eval for remote-agent-create (and both sibling checks remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-15T23:39:57Z because POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with error code "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The swarm backend rejected the eval's agent creation request before any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) could be collected, causing a total contract gap across all three remote-agents checks.
investigation.rootCause: The production swarm backend enforces a hard per-org agent quota of 100. At the time the eval ran, the org used by the observability probe had already reached that limit, so POST /api/agents returned 409 "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" immediately. Because agent creation is the first step in the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1314: createAgent(args, track, "remote", null, orgId)), no downstream evidence (vmIdPresent, remoteState, agentId) was ever written, and all three remote-agents checks failed with the identical error message. This is an eval infrastructure failure caused by a resource-limit condition in the production API; no evidence of a user-facing outage or product regression is present in the packet.
proof: failed-check.message: POST /api/agents failed with 409 — error body contains 'conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the swarm backend rejected the creation request before any agent was provisioned.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}), confirming zero evidence keys were written — consistent with the runner aborting at the createAgent call before any evidence could be recorded.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing, confirming the probe never progressed past the initial API call.

sibling.remote-agent-state and sibling.remote-agent-runtime: both siblings carry the identical 409 message (sameMessage: true), indicating all three checks share the same upstream failure point — the createAgent call at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1314.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1306-1314: runner code shows createAgent is called immediately after requireOrgId, meaning a 409 at that call terminates the probe before any evidence is emitted.
verifierContext.siblingCorrelation.likelySharedDependencyFailure: true — verifier independently flagged a shared dependency failure across all three checks.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — Org-level swarm agent quota exhausted: The observability probe's org account has accumulated 100 remote agents (the enforced limit) from prior eval runs, leaving no capacity for new agent creation. This is the most evidence-supported cause given the explicit quota error in failed-check.message.

SECONDARY — Eval cleanup (withCleanup) failed to delete agents from a previous run: The runner wraps creation in withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1312), which is responsible for deleting eval-created agents. If a prior run crashed or cleanup was skipped, leaked agents could accumulate toward the quota limit over time.

TERTIARY — Observability probe org is shared with non-eval workloads: If the org used by the probe is also used for real or test agents outside the eval harness, external agents could be consuming quota slots independently of the eval lifecycle.

LOW CONFIDENCE — Commit 23a7506 ('fix(observability): propagate scheduled process model') touched all three implicated eval files approximately 6 minutes before the failure (committed 23:33:22Z, eval ran 23:39:56Z); however, 23a7506's touched paths are CI/workflow files with no candidate paths matching the eval runner or quota logic, and matchedNeedles is empty — this commit is not supported as causal by the available evidence.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on production-api — Agent Runtime Harness Unreachable
investigations.summary: The AURA observability eval for `image-generation-stream` in the `production-api` runtime environment failed because the agent runtime harness returned a 404, causing a `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` error immediately after `generation_start`. This is an eval infrastructure failure localized to the `production-api` harness endpoint; the identical check passed in the `desktop-release` environment at the same run time, confirming the image generation feature itself is not broadly broken.
investigations.rootCause: The eval runner (`infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs`, line 1413) issued an SSE request to `/api/generate/image/stream` against the `production-api` harness target. The harness responded with HTTP 404, surfaced as `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED`. This caused the stream to terminate after `generation_start` with a `generation_error` frame, producing no `generation_completed` frame and no image URL — leaving both required evidence keys (`frameTypes`, `imageUrlPresent`) absent. The failure is scoped to the `production-api` harness reachability or routing configuration, not to the image generation feature as a whole. The root cause is uncertain between: (a) the `production-api` harness is not deployed or is deployed at a URL that does not match the configured `LOCAL_HARNESS_URL` / `SWARM_BASE_URL`, or (b) the harness is deployed but the `/api/generate/image/stream` route is missing or incompatible in the version currently running there.
proof: failed-check.evidence: stream emitted event=generation_error with code=SESSION_OPEN_FAILED and message 'agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version.'
failed-check.message: 'Missing expected evidence: frameTypes, imageUrlPresent' — both required evidence keys are absent because the stream never reached generation_completed.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=2032, far below the warningLatencyMs=180000 threshold, confirming the request failed immediately rather than timing out — consistent with a 404 rather than a slow or hung backend.

sibling.image-generation-stream: the same check in runtimeEnvironment=desktop-release passed at endedAt=2026-06-15T23:39:42.316Z with evidenceKeys=[frameTypes, imageUrlPresent] and imageUrlPresent=true, ruling out a shared upstream image generation service outage.
source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1406-1414: runner calls apiSse(args, '/api/generate/image/stream', ...) — the 404 is returned from this endpoint on the production-api target.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:237-245: the production-api check is registered as required=false with statusImpact=informational, meaning this is an eval-level signal, not a declared production outage indicator.
possibleCauses: Most likely: The production-api harness is not deployed, is deployed at a different URL than what LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL resolves to in the observability workflow, causing every request to return 404 before any session can open.

Second: The production-api harness is deployed but is running an incompatible version that does not expose the /api/generate/image/stream route, or the route was renamed or removed in the version currently deployed.

Third (hypothesis, low confidence): Commit 23a7506 ('fix(observability): propagate scheduled process model') touched .github/workflows/aura-observability.yml and .github/actions/setup-harness-sibling/action.yml — it is possible a workflow or harness-setup change altered how the production-api harness URL is injected or how the harness sibling is started, but this is unproven because 23a7506's candidateTouchedPaths is empty and no eval or source evidence directly links it to the 404 (suspect-change.23a7506 confidence=low).

Fourth: The access token (args.token) is present (the runner did not return SKIP), but the token may be scoped or routed to a different environment than the production-api harness, causing the harness to reject the session-open request with 404.
